CMR-LOI-90-035::0012.reference_en: Law No. 90/035 of 10 August 1990 (pharmacist profession), Sections 13 and 14
CMR-LOI-90-035::0012.texte_en: Section 13.- The following shall be reserved to pharmacists: a) the preparation of: articles and medicines intended for use in human medicine; dressing materials [and … — illegible in the OCR source] presented as conforming to the pharmacopoeia; insecticides and acaricides intended to be applied to humans; products intended for the maintenance or application of contact lenses; products and reagents packaged for sale to the public which, without being covered by Section 15 below, are nevertheless intended for medical diagnosis; b) wholesale, retail sale and any supply to the public of the products and articles listed in the preceding paragraph; c) the sale of medicinal plants listed in the pharmacopoeia; d) the importation, holding and commercial exploitation of all the products referred to in this Section. [The fragment continues with Section 14, whose heading is badly recognised:] Section 14.- The preparation and supply of vaccines, sera and allergens, where they are specially prepared for a single individual, may be carried out by any person approved by the authority responsible for public health.

CMR-LOI-90-035::0013.reference_en: Law No. 90/035 of 10 August 1990 (pharmacist profession), Section 15
CMR-LOI-90-035::0013.texte_en: Section 15.- (1) A medicine shall mean any substance or composition presented as having curative or preventive properties with regard to human or animal diseases, as well as any product that may be administered to humans or animals with a view to making a medical diagnosis or to restoring, correcting or modifying their organic functions. (2) The following shall in particular be considered as medicines: products containing a substance having a therapeutic action within the meaning of subsection 1 above or containing poisonous substances at non-exempted doses and concentrations; dietetic products which contain in their composition chemical or biological substances that do not themselves constitute foods, but whose presence gives these products either special properties sought in dietetic therapy or the properties of test meals. (3) Products used for disinfecting premises and for dental prostheses shall not be considered as medicines.

CMR-LOI-90-035::0014.reference_en: Law No. 90/035 of 10 August 1990 (pharmacist profession), Section 16
CMR-LOI-90-035::0014.texte_en: Section 16.- Whoever knowingly carries out operations reserved to pharmacists without meeting the conditions laid down by this law shall be liable to a fine of five hundred thousand (500 000) to two million (2 000 000) CFA francs and to imprisonment of six (06) days to six (06) months, or to only one of these two penalties. The court shall, in addition, order the closure of the establishment and the confiscation of all articles, medicines and substances used to support this irregular activity. [Chapter heading that follows in the fragment:] Chapter 4 – Prohibition of certain agreements between pharmacists and members of certain professions.

CMR-LOI-90-035::0017.reference_en: Law No. 90/035 of 10 August 1990 (pharmacist profession), Section 19
CMR-LOI-90-035::0017.texte_en: Section 19.- Advertising concerning medicines and pharmaceutical establishments shall be authorised only under the conditions laid down by the supervising authority after consultation of the Council of the Order of Pharmacists.

CMR-LOI-90-035::0049.reference_en: Law No. 90/035 of 10 August 1990 (pharmacist profession), Section 52
CMR-LOI-90-035::0049.texte_en: Section 52.- The sale to the public of any medicines, products and accessories referred to in Section 15 above through commercial houses, purchasing groups or establishments owned or managed by persons who do not hold the pharmacist's diploma shall be prohibited, with the exception of those provided for in Section 37.

CMR-LOI-90-035::0050.reference_en: Law No. 90/035 of 10 August 1990 (pharmacist profession), Section 53
CMR-LOI-90-035::0050.texte_en: Section 53.- Any [sale — the source reads « délit », probably « débit »], display or distribution of medicines on the public highway, at fairs [and] markets is prohibited to any person, even one holding the pharmacist's diploma.

CMR-LOI-90-035::0072.reference_en: Law No. 90/035 of 10 August 1990 (pharmacist profession), Section 75
CMR-LOI-90-035::0072.texte_en: Section 75.- It shall be prohibited for any person to engage in acts likely to cause or facilitate abortion, namely: displaying, offering, selling, putting up for sale, having sold, distributing or having distributed in any manner whatsoever, remedies and substances, « intra-urinaires » probes [as printed in the source] and other similar articles; making speeches in public places or meetings; selling, putting up for sale, offering, even by non-public means, displaying, posting, distributing on the public highway or in public places, distributing at home, handing over under wrapper or in an envelope, closed or not, to the post or to any other agent for the distribution or transport, books, writings, printed matter, announcements, posters, drawings, images or emblems; advertising medical or so-called medical practices [the fragment ends here].

CMR-LOI-2010-012::0034.reference_en: Law No. 2010/012 of 21 December 2010 (cybersecurity and cybercrime), Section 29
CMR-LOI-2010-012::0034.texte_en: Section 29.- (1) Operators of information systems shall be required to retain the connection and traffic data of their information systems for a period of ten (10) years. (2) Operators of information systems shall install mechanisms for monitoring access control to the data of their information systems. The data retained may be accessed during judicial investigations. (3) The facilities of operators of information systems may be searched or seized on the order of a judicial authority under the conditions provided for by the laws and regulations in force.
